sections.heading: Living World & Binomial Nomenclature (ICBN / ICZN)
sections.summary: Carolus Linnaeus introduced binomial nomenclature (Genus capitalized + specific epithet lowercase, italicized/underlined separately).
keyPoints: Taxonomic hierarchy ascending: Species -> Genus -> Family -> Order -> Class -> Phylum/Division -> Kingdom.
As we move higher toward Kingdom, number of common shared characters DECREASES.
Mango = Mangifera indica; Wheat = Triticum aestivum (Poaceae); Housefly = Musca domestica (Muscidae); Man = Homo sapiens.

sections.heading: Whittaker Five Kingdoms & Non-Cellular Agents
sections.summary: Criteria: Cell structure, Body organization, Mode of nutrition, Reproduction & Phylogenetic relationships.
keyPoints: Monera: Archaebacteria (branched ether lipids survive extreme habitats: Methanogens in marshy/rumen gut, Halophiles, Thermoacidophiles); Mycoplasma lacks cell wall & survives without O2!

Protista: Chrysophytes (Diatoms -> indestructible siliceous soap-box cell walls -> diatomaceous earth), Dinoflagellates (Gonyaulax red tide), Euglenoids (pellicle protein layer), Slime Moulds, Protozoans.

Fungi: Phycomycetes (aseptate coenocytic: Rhizopus, Albugo), Ascomycetes (sac fungi, Neurospora genetic workhorse, Penicillium), Basidiomycetes (clamp connections, Agaricus, Puccinia), Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi, sexual stage absent: Alternaria, Trichoderma).

Viruses (obligate parasites, TMV ssRNA, Bacteriophage dsDNA); Viroids (T.O. Diener 1971 -> free low-MW infectious RNA WITHOUT protein coat -> Potato spindle tuber!); Prions (folded infectious protein -> BSE/CJD).

sections.heading: Plant Kingdom: Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes & Gymnosperms
sections.summary: Life-cycle alternation shifts from haploid-dominant (Algae & Bryophytes) to sporophyte-dominant (Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms).
keyPoints: Chlorophyceae (Chl a,b; Starch; 2-8 equal apical flagella), Phaeophyceae (Chl a,c + Fucoxanthin; Mannitol/Laminarin; Algin; 2 unequal lateral), Rhodophyceae (Chl a,d + Phycoerythrin; Floridean starch; Agar/Carrageen; NO flagella!).

Bryophytes (amphibians of plant kingdom): dominant gametophyte; Sphagnum peat moss. Pteridophytes: first vascular terrestrial plants; Selaginella & Salvinia show HETEROSPORY (precursor to seed habit!).
Gymnosperms (naked seeds): Cycas (unbranched stem, coralloid roots with N2-fixing Anabaena) vs Pinus (branched, mycorrhizal roots, winged pollen).

formulas.formula: Green: Starch (a,b) | Brown: Mannitol/Laminarin (a,c,Fucoxanthin) | Red: Floridean (a,d,Phycoerythrin)
formulas.note: Rhodophyceae (Polysiphonia/Porphyra/Gracilaria) completely lack motile flagellated gametes!
Deuteromycetes lack known sexual spores — moved once sexual stage found

traps: Bacteriophages usually carry dsDNA whereas plant viruses like TMV carry ssRNA — NEVER swap these!
Bryophyte sporophyte is NOT free-living; it stays attached to and nourished by the dominant photosynthetic gametophyte! In Pteridophytes, both gametophyte (prothallus) & sporophyte are independent!

solvedExamples.question: Which pair of pteridophytes exhibits heterospory (producing both microspores and megaspores), acting as evolutionary precursor to seed habit?
steps: Recall NCERT Class XI Ch 3 Pteridophytes: most pteridophytes (Dryopteris, Pteris, Equisetum) are homosporous.
ONLY genera like Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Polysiphonia, Laminaria & Chara are algae; Sphagnum & Funaria are bryophytes.

sections.heading: Morphology: Phyllotaxy, Aestivation, Placentation & Fruit
sections.summary: Diagnostic floral terms classify angiosperms rapidly for NEET statement questions.
keyPoints: Aestivation: Valvate (Calotropis), Twisted (China rose, Lady's finger, Cotton), Imbricate (Cassia, Gulmohar), Vexillary/Papilionaceous (Pea, Bean — 1 standard + 2 wings + 2 fused keel).
Placentation: Marginal (Pea), Axile (China rose, Tomato, Lemon), Parietal (Mustard, Argemone — false septum replum!), Free Central (Dianthus, Primrose), Basal (Sunflower, Marigold).
Ovary Position: Hypogynous Superior (Mustard, China rose, Brinjal); Perigynous Half-Inferior (Plum, Rose, Peach); Epigynous Inferior (Guava, Cucumber, Ray florets of Sunflower).

sections.heading: NMC Updated Plant Families Key Diagnostics
sections.summary: Master floral symmetry, stamens, and fruit types across the 5 official NMC families.
keyPoints: Malvaceae (China rose, Cotton, Bhindi): Epicalyx present, Monoadelphous stamens (stamina tube around style), Reniform monothecous anthers, Twisted corolla, Axile placentation.
Brassicaceae / Cruciferae (Mustard, Radish): Cruciform 4 petals, Tetradynamous stamens (2 short outer + 4 long inner = A_(2+4)), Parietal placentation with false septum (replum), Siliqua fruit.
Fabaceae / Leguminosae (Pea, Gram): Zygomorphic, Vexillary aestivation, Diadelphous stamens A_(9)+1, Marginal placentation, Legume pod.
Asteraceae / Compositae (Sunflower, Marigold): Capitulum (Head) inflorescence, Syngenesious anthers (fused anthers, free filaments), Pappus hairy calyx, Basal single ovule, Cypsela fruit.
Poaceae / Gramineae (Wheat, Maize, Rice): Spikelet inflorescence, Perianth reduced to Lodicules, Versatile anthers, Feathery stigma, Basal placentation, Caryopsis fruit!

sections.heading: Plant Anatomy: Vascular Bundles & Secondary Tissue Maps
sections.summary: Compare Dicot vs Monocot internal histology carefully.
keyPoints: Endarch protoxylem = Stems; Exarch protoxylem = Roots. Radial bundles = Roots; Conjoint = Stems & Leaves.

Dicot Stem: Hypodermis collenchymatous, ring vascular bundles (conjoint, collateral, OPEN with cambium), well-developed pith. Monocot Stem: Hypodermis sclerenchymatous, scattered CLOSED vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath + water-containing cavities.
Dicot Root: Tetrarch (2-4 xylem patches), pith small/absent. Monocot Root: Polyarch (>6 xylem), large pith! Isobilateral monocot leaf carries Bulliform cells (curl leaves to minimize transpiration!).

formulas.note: Tetradynamous stamens (4 long + 2 short) + Replum septum!
Vexillary corolla + Diadelphous 9+1 stamens!
Wheat/Rice/Maize scutellum = single shield-shaped cotyledon

comparison.title: NMC Five Angiosperm Families Cheat Matrix

Parietal ovary starts 1-chambered but turns 2-chambered due to false septum (Replum) specifically in Mustard/Brassicaceae!

solvedExamples.question: A flower exhibits epicalyx, monoadelphous stamens forming a stamina column, twisted aestivation, and axile placentation. Identify its family.

sections.heading: Cell: Prokaryotes, Biomembranes & Endomembrane Organelles
sections.summary: Singer & Nicolson Fluid Mosaic Model (1972) describes quasi-fluid phospholipid bilayer allowing lateral protein diffusion.
keyPoints: Endomembrane System (coordinated functions): ER + Golgi apparatus + Lysosomes + Vacuoles (Mitochondria, Chloroplasts & Peroxisomes are EXCLUDED!).
Rough ER (ribosomes) -> protein synthesis; Smooth ER -> lipid/steroid hormone synthesis; Golgi cis (forming/convex) -> trans (maturing/concave) packages glycoproteins & glycolipids.
Mitochondria & Chloroplasts are semi-autonomous with 70S ribosomes + circular dsDNA. Centrioles = 9+0 microtubule triplets; Cilia/Flagella = 9+2 axoneme.

sections.heading: Cell Cycle & Meiosis I Prophase-I Substages
sections.summary: Track Chromosome number (N vs 2N) separately from DNA content (2C vs 4C) carefully across every checkpoint!
keyPoints: S-phase (Synthesis): DNA DOUBLES (2C -> 4C) and centrioles duplicate in cytoplasm, YET chromosome number (2N) remains UNCHANGED!
Metaphase: best stage to study chromosome morphology (chromosomes aligned on equatorial plate). Anaphase: centromere splits -> chromatids move to opposite poles.

Prophase-I Order (L-Z-P-D-D): Leptotene (compaction) -> Zygotene (Synapsis / Synaptonemal complex -> Bivalents) -> Pachytene (Crossing over via RECOMBINASE!) -> Diplotene (Chiasmata X-shapes, oocyte arrest months/years!) -> Diakinesis (Terminalisation of chiasmata).

formulas.note: Centromeres split ONLY in Mitotic Anaphase & Meiosis II Anaphase-II (NEVER Anaphase-I!)
Human 2n=46 forms 23 bivalents (92 chromatids) in Pachytene!

traps: Crossing over happens between NON-SISTER chromatids of homologous chromosomes in PACHYTENE (NOT sister chromatids!).
Mitosis/G2 keeps chromosome count 2N identical to G1 even though DNA quantity doubles to 4C!

solvedExamples.question: If a diploid pollen mother cell has 2n = 24 chromosomes and 20 pg DNA at G1 phase, find chromosome number and DNA after S-phase and after Meiosis-I.
steps: After S-phase (G2): Chromosomes STAY 24 (2n), DNA DOUBLES to 40 pg.
After Meiosis-I (telophase-I): Homologous chromosomes segregate -> n = 12 chromosomes, DNA = 20 pg per daughter nucleus.
solvedExamples.answer: G2: 24 ch, 40 pg | Post Meiosis-I: 12 ch, 20 pg
solvedExamples.pitfall: DNA drops from 40 -> 20 -> 10 pg across Meiosis I and II!

sections.heading: Photosynthesis: Light Reaction, C3 Calvin & C4 Hatch-Slack
sections.summary: Light reactions on thylakoid membranes split water (Mn^2+, Cl^-) on PS-II lumen side and generate ATP + NADPH driving stroma CO2 fixation.
keyPoints: PS-II (P680) drives non-cyclic Z-scheme (ATP + NADPH + O2); PS-I (P700) alone drives cyclic photophosphorylation (ONLY ATP, NO NADPH/O2).
C3 Calvin Cycle (all plants, RuBisCO): fixing 1 CO2 needs 3 ATP + 2 NADPH; 1 Glucose (6 CO2) costs 18 ATP + 12 NADPH. Photorespiration (C2) wastes 25% fixed C in Chloroplast-Peroxisome-Mitochondria!

C4 Kranz Anatomy (Maize, Sugarcane, Sorghum): Mesophyll uses PEPcase (ZERO oxygenase waste!) -> 4C OAA -> Malate -> Bundle Sheath RuBisCO -> costs 30 ATP + 12 NADPH per glucose (5 ATP/CO2) with zero photorespiration!

sections.heading: Cellular Respiration: Glycolysis, Krebs & ETS
sections.summary: Glucose oxidizes cleanly across Cytosol (EMP Glycolysis) and Mitochondrial Matrix (Krebs Cycle) + Inner Membrane (ETS Complex I-V).
keyPoints: Glycolysis (Universal in anaerobes & aerobes, Cytoplasm): Glucose -> 2 Pyruvate + 2 net ATP + 2 NADH (10 steps; Hexokinase & PFK pacemaker steps!).
Link + Krebs Cycle (Matrix): Per glucose (2 Acetyl-CoA): 2 GTP (ATP) + 6 NADH + 2 FADH2 + 4 CO2 (plus 2 NADH from Link = total 38 or 36 net ATP aerobic vs only 2 ATP fermentation!).
Respiratory Quotient RQ: Carbohydrates = 1.0; Fats (Tripalmitin) = 0.7; Proteins = 0.9; Succulents (CAM) = 0; Anaerobic = infinity.

sections.heading: Plant Growth Regulators (PGRs)
sections.summary: Growth promoters (Auxin, GA, Cytokinin) vs Inhibitors/Stress (ABA, Ethylene).
keyPoints: Auxin (IAA/IBA/2,4-D): Apical dominance, rooting in stem cuttings, 2,4-D kills dicot weeds selectively leaving monocot lawns.
Gibberellins (GA3): Bolting in rosette cabbage/beet, increases sugarcane stem length (+20 tonnes/acre), malting in brewing.
Cytokinin (Kinetin/Zeatin): Overcomes apical dominance, delays leaf senescence (Richmond-Lang effect).
Ethylene (Gaseous): Triple response, fruit ripening, femaleness in cucumber, thinning cotton/cherry. ABA: Stomatal closure stress hormone, seed dormancy (antagonist to GA).

formulas.formula: C3: 18 ATP + 12 NADPH | C4: 30 ATP + 12 NADPH
formulas.note: C4 pays 2 extra ATP per CO2 to pump/regenerate PEP and avoid photorespiration

formulas.formula: RQ = Volume CO2 evolved / Volume O2 consumed
formulas.note: Carbs = 1.0, Tripalmitin fat = 0.7, Organic acids > 1 (Oxalic = 4.0)

comparison.title: C3 vs C4 Plants Summary Matrix

traps: O2 evolution during photosynthesis occurs strictly on the INNER LUMEN side of thylakoid membrane via PS-II Mn-protein complex, NEVER PS-I!
Complex IV of mitochondrial ETS is Cytochrome c Oxidase containing TWO copper centres (Cu_A, Cu_B) + Cytochromes a & a3 — favorite NEET trap!

solvedExamples.question: How many turns of the Calvin cycle and total ATP + NADPH molecules are consumed to synthesize ONE molecule of Sucrose (12 carbons)?
steps: 1 Glucose (6C) needs 6 Calvin turns = 18 ATP + 12 NADPH.
Sucrose is a disaccharide of 12 carbons (12 CO2 fixed) -> requires 12 Calvin turns.
Total = 36 ATP + 24 NADPH.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Always verify whether question asks per CO2 (3 ATP, 2 NADPH), per Glucose (18, 12), or per Sucrose (36, 24)!

sections.heading: Microsporogenesis, Megasporogenesis & Embryo Sac (7-Celled, 8-Nucleate)
sections.summary: Anther wall layers (Epidermis -> Endothecium -> Middle layers -> Tapetum [polyploid, dense cytoplasm nourishing pollen!]).
keyPoints: Sporopollenin forms resistant exine EXCEPT at germ pores. 60% angiosperms shed pollen at 2-celled stage (vegetative + generative); 40% at 3-celled stage.

Monosporic Polygonum embryo sac: 1 functional megaspore undergoes 3 sequential free-nuclear mitoses -> 7 cells, 8 nuclei (3 antipodals + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus + 1 egg + 1 large central cell with 2 polar nuclei!).

sections.heading: Pollination, Outbreeding Devices, Double Fertilisation & Seed
sections.summary: Outbreeding devices (Dichogamy, Herkogamy, Self-Incompatibility, Dioecy) prevent selfing inbreeding depression.
keyPoints: Double Fertilisation (unique to Angiosperms): Syngamy (Egg n + Male n -> Zygote 2n) + Triple Fusion (2 Polar Nuclei n+n + Male n -> Primary Endosperm Nucleus PEN 3n).
Albuminous/Endospermic seeds (Wheat, Maize, Castor, Coconut) vs Exalbuminous/Non-endospermic (Pea, Groundnut, Beans).
Apomixis mimics sexual reproduction WITHOUT fertilisation (Asteraceae, grasses); Polyembryony (Citrus, Mango).

formulas.formula: Meiosis for N pollen = N/4 ; N eggs = N ; N seeds = N + N/4 = 5N/4
formulas.note: 100 wheat grains require 100 + 25 = 125 meiotic divisions!

formulas.formula: Endosperm = 2 x Female Gamete (n_F) + 1 x Male Gamete (n_M)
formulas.note: 4n female x 2n male -> female polar = 2n+2n=4n, male=1n => 5n endosperm!

comparison.title: Seed & Fruit Special Structures
rows: Triple fusion (PEN); Coconut water (free-nuclear) & white kernel (cellular)
Thalamus forms fleshy part (Apple, Strawberry, Cashew)

traps: Castor has albuminous (endospermic) dicot seed, while Orchid is non-endospermic monocot — NEVER treat dicot = non-endospermic as 100% rule!
Papaya is DIOECIOUS (prevents BOTH autogamy AND geitonogamy); Castor/Maize are MONOECIOUS (prevent autogamy but NOT geitonogamy!).

solvedExamples.question: If a tetraploid (4n) female flowering plant is crossed with a diploid (2n) male plant, determine ploidy of Zygote and Endosperm.
steps: Female gamete (egg & each polar nucleus) = 4n / 2 = 2n.
Male gamete = 2n / 2 = n.
Zygote = 2n + n = 3n; Endosperm = (2n + 2n) + n = 5n.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Never assume endosperm is ALWAYS 3n — compute (2 x egg ploidy + sperm ploidy)!

sections.heading: Mendelian Genetics, Linkage Maps & Chromosomal Disorders
sections.summary: Exceptions to Mendel: Incomplete Dominance (Snapdragon 1:2:1), Co-dominance (ABO blood I^A I^B), Pleiotropy (PKU single gene -> multiple defects), Polygenic (Skin colour, Kernel).
keyPoints: Drosophila linkage (T.H. Morgan): tight yellow-white (1.3% recombination) vs loose white-miniature wing (37.2%); 1% recombination = 1 map unit (cM).
Sex Determination: XX-XY (Human, Drosophila male heterogametic), XX-XO (Grasshopper), ZZ-ZW (Birds female heterogametic!), Haplodiploidy (Honeybee).

Mendelian Disorders: Haemophilia, Colour blindness (X-linked recessive criscross!), Sickle-cell anaemia (autosomal recessive GAG -> GUG, Glu -> Val at 6th beta-globin), Phenylketonuria, Thalassemia. Chromosomal: Down (Trisomy 21), Klinefelter (47 XXY), Turner (45 X0).

sections.heading: Molecular Basis: DNA Replication, Transcription & Lac Operon
sections.summary: Central Dogma (Crick): DNA --(Replication)--> DNA --(Transcription)--> mRNA --(Translation)--> Protein.
keyPoints: Chargaff Law (dsDNA ONLY): [A] = [T], [G] = [C]; %G = %C => %A + %T = 100 - (%G + %C). Length = Base pairs x 0.34 nm (~2.2 m in human 6.6 x 10^9 bp).
Semi-conservative Replication (Meselson & Stahl 15N): DNA polymerase ALWAYS adds dNTPs 5' -> 3' (Leading continuous; Lagging discontinuous Okazaki fragments joined by DNA Ligase).
Transcription uses RNA Pol I (rRNA 28S/18S/5.8S), II (hnRNA -> mRNA), III (tRNA, 5S rRNA, snRNA). Splicing removes INTRONS keeping EXONS! Capping (mGppp 5'), Tailing (poly-A 3').

Genetic Code: 64 codons (61 sense + 3 stop UAA/UAG/UGA); AUG = Start + Methionine; Universal & Degenerate. Lac Operon (Jacob-Monod): z(beta-gal), y(permease), a(transacetylase) — NEGATIVE regulation by repressor unless ALLOLACTOSE inducer binds!

formulas.note: n = number of heterozygous loci (AaBbCc has n=3 -> 8 gametes)

formulas.formula: Skipped gen = Recessive | Father->Daughter 100% = X-Linked Dom | Mother->All Sons = X-Linked Rec
formulas.note: Unaffected parents having affected daughter -> MUST be Autosomal Recessive!

comparison.title: Human Chromosomal Disorders Matrix

Tall sterile male, Gynaecomastia (feminine breast development)

traps: Remember in Lac Operon, the actual physiological inducer binding the lac repressor is ALLOLACTOSE (or lactose); glucose drops cAMP turning off high transcription!
DNA-dependent RNA polymerase transcribes ONLY one template strand (3' -> 5') creating mRNA identical to CODING strand (5' -> 3') EXCEPT U replaces T!

solvedExamples.question: If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 18% Cytosine, find the percentage of Adenine.
steps: By Chargaff's equivalence: [G] = [C] = 18% => G + C = 36%.
Remaining A + T = 100% - 36% = 64%.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Chargaff base pairing applies ONLY to double-stranded DNA (fails for ssDNA or ssRNA phages like Phi X 174!).

Pyramids: Energy is ALWAYS UPRIGHT; Sea Biomass pyramid is INVERTED (phytoplankton < zooplankton/fishes); Tree Number pyramid is inverted/spindle.

Species-Area Relationship (Alexander von Humboldt): log S = log C + Z log A (typical Z = 0.1-0.2; entire continents Z = 0.6-1.2!). In-situ (National Parks, 34 Hotspots [3 in India: Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma, Himalaya]) vs Ex-situ (Seed banks, Cryopreservation -196 deg C).

sections.heading: Biomolecules: Proteins, Lipids & Secondary Metabolites
sections.summary: Acid-insoluble pool contains macromolecules (>1000 Da: Proteins, Nucleic Acids, Polysaccharides) PLUS Lipids (<800 Da membrane vesicles!).
keyPoints: Amino acids: Acidic (Glutamic, Aspartic), Basic (Lysine, Arginine), Neutral (Valine), Aromatic (Tyrosine, Tryptophan, Phenylalanine); Cysteine contains Sulphur; Glycine has NO chiral carbon.

Protein structures: Primary (peptide sequence), Secondary (alpha-helix, beta-pleated H-bonds), Tertiary (disulphide/hydrophobic 3D fold — mandatory for biological enzyme activity!), Quaternary (Haemoglobin 2 alpha + 2 beta).
Secondary Metabolites: Alkaloids (Morphine, Codeine), Terpenoids (Monoterpenes), Toxins (Abrin, Ricin), Lectins (Concanavalin A), Drugs (Vinblastin, Curcumin).

sections.heading: Enzyme Kinetics & Competitive Inhibition
sections.summary: Enzymes lower Activation Energy barrier WITHOUT altering Delta G equilibrium.
keyPoints: Michaelis constant K_m = [Substrate] at which reaction reaches V_max / 2 (lower K_m = higher enzyme affinity!).

Competitive Inhibition (e.g. Malonate inhibiting Succinate Dehydrogenase): Inhibitor mimics substrate & binds active site -> V_max stays UNCHANGED (overcome by flooding substrate!), apparent K_m INCREASES!
Ribozyme = catalytic RNA enzyme (non-protein!). Prosthetic group (Haem covalently/tightly bound) vs Coenzyme (NAD/NADP from Niacin vitamin).

formulas.note: Classic NCERT graph: curve shifts right yet approaches identical V_max plateau!

formulas.formula: Animal World: Collagen | Whole Biosphere: RuBisCO
formulas.note: Frequently tested 1-liner from NCERT Table

traps: Lipids are STRICTLY NOT macromolecules (<800 Da molecular weight), yet they appear in the acid-insoluble fraction because cell membranes shatter into water-insoluble vesicles!
Inulin is a polymer of FRUCTOSE (unlike Insulin which is a peptide hormone!); Chitin = polymer of N-acetylglucosamine (NAG).

solvedExamples.question: Malonate closely resembles succinate structurally and inhibits succinate dehydrogenase. How do K_m and V_max behave if excess succinate is added?
steps: Competitive inhibition keeps V_max unchanged because excess succinate outcompetes malonate.
Higher substrate concentration is needed to achieve V_max/2, so K_m increases.
solvedExamples.pitfall: In non-competitive inhibition, V_max drops while K_m stays unchanged.

sections.heading: Breathing, Lung Capacities & Oxygen Dissociation Curve
sections.summary: Inspiration is active (diaphragm flattens + external intercostals lift ribs, lowering intrapulmonary pressure below atmospheric); normal expiration is passive.
keyPoints: Lung Volumes (mL): TV = 500, IRV = 2500-3000, ERV = 1000-1100, RV = 1100-1200 (cannot be measured directly by simple spirometer!).
Capacities: IC = TV+IRV; EC = TV+ERV; FRC = ERV+RV; VC = ERV+TV+IRV; TLC = VC+RV.

Sigmoid O2-Hb Curve: Right shift (Bohr Effect -> O2 dissociation favored in tissues!) caused by LOW pO2, HIGH pCO2, HIGH H+ (low pH), HIGH Temp! CO2 moves 70% as HCO3^- (chloride shift), 20-25% carbaminohaemoglobin, 7% dissolved.

sections.heading: Blood Clotting, Cardiac Cycle & ECG Waves
sections.summary: Human heart (myogenic, SA node pacemaker ~70-75/min) completes one Cardiac Cycle in 0.8 s (Stroke Volume ~70 mL -> Cardiac Output ~5 L/min).
keyPoints: Sounds: Lub (1st, ventricular systole start -> AV tricuspid/bicuspid closure); Dub (2nd, ventricular diastole start -> semilunar valves closure).
ECG P-QRS-T: P wave = Atrial depolarization (systole follows); QRS complex = Ventricular depolarization (counts heart rate!); T wave = Ventricular repolarization.
Blood Clotting: Prothrombin --(Thrombokinase, Ca^2+)--> Thrombin; Fibrinogen -> insoluble Fibrin meshwork.

formulas.formula: VC = IRV + TV + ERV = TLC - RV
formulas.note: Simple spirometer CANNOT measure Residual Volume RV, FRC, or TLC!

formulas.formula: CO = Stroke Volume x Heart Rate (~70 mL x 72/min = 5040 mL)
formulas.note: Athletes boost CO cleanly by raising stroke volume

traps: Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs when Rh-NEGATIVE mother carries Rh-POSITIVE foetus in her SECOND pregnancy (prevented by anti-Rh antibodies RhoGAM immediately after 1st delivery)!
Right shift of O2-Hb curve means LOWER affinity (UNLOADING at tissues); Fetal Hb curve lies to the LEFT of adult Hb!

solvedExamples.question: Calculate Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) and Vital Capacity (VC) if TV = 500 mL, IRV = 2800 mL, ERV = 1000 mL, RV = 1200 mL.
solvedExamples.pitfall: Expiratory Capacity (EC = TV + ERV = 1500 mL) != Functional Residual Capacity (FRC = ERV + RV)!

sections.heading: Excretion (Counter-Current & RAAS) + Locomotion (Sarcomere)
sections.summary: Juxtamedullary nephrons + vasa recta build a 300 -> 1200 mOsmol/L medullary osmolarity gradient via NaCl & Urea counter-current exchange.
keyPoints: PCT reabsorbs 70-80% electrolytes/water + 100% glucose/amino acids (cuboidal brush-border epithelium); DCT conditional reabsorption regulated by Aldosterone & ADH.
RAAS: Low GFR -> JG cells release Renin -> Angiotensinogen -> Ang I -> Ang II (vasoconstrictor + stimulates Adrenal Cortex Aldosterone!). ANF from heart atria acts OPPOSITE as vasodilator check!

Sarcomere (Z-line to Z-line): During contraction, H-zone & I-band SHORTEN/disappear while A-band stays CONSTANT length! Ca^2+ binds Troponin TpC exposing myosin-binding sites on actin; ATP hydrolysis resets myosin head.

sections.heading: Neural Conduction & Endocrine Disorders
sections.summary: Resting neuron maintains -70 mV via 3 Na^+ out / 2 K^+ in ATPase pump; action potential depolarizes via rapid Na^+ influx.
keyPoints: Repolarization restores negative interior via voltage-gated K^+ efflux. Chemical synapse transfers signal across cleft via Ca^2+-triggered Acetylcholine vesicle fusion.
Anterior Pituitary (GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH, FSH) vs Posterior Pituitary stores Hypothalamic Oxytocin & Vasopressin (ADH).

Hormone Mechanisms: Peptide/Protein (Insulin, FSH, Glucagon) bind membrane receptors generating 2nd messengers (cAMP, IP3, Ca^2+); Steroid/Thyroid (Cortisol, Testosterone, T4) cross membrane & bind intracellular nuclear receptors altering DNA transcription!

formulas.note: 99% filtrate reabsorbed -> ~1.5 L urine excreted daily
Axial = 80 bones + Appendicular = 126 = 206 total!

comparison.title: Critical Endocrine Disorders & Causes
rows: Inability of kidneys to conserve water -> dilute polyuria (NO glucose in urine!)
Enlarged thyroid, protruding eyeballs, elevated BMR
Low cortisol/aldosterone -> fatigue, hypoglycemia, altered carbs

traps: A-band length NEVER shortens during skeletal muscle contraction — ONLY I-band and H-zone shorten as thin filaments slide inward!
ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor) is the ONLY major vasodilating peptide checking/opposing RAAS blood pressure rise!

solvedExamples.question: Which group of hormones acts directly on nuclear genome transcription via intracellular receptors WITHOUT generating cAMP second messengers?
steps: Lipid-soluble steroid hormones (Cortisol, Testosterone, Estradiol, Progesterone) and iodothyronines (T3/T4) diffuse through lipid bilayer.
Water-soluble peptide hormones (FSH, Insulin, Epinephrine) remain outside and require cAMP/IP3/Ca^2+.
solvedExamples.answer: Steroid hormones (Cortisol, Estrogen, Testosterone) & Thyroid hormones (T3/T4)
solvedExamples.pitfall: Remember Epinephrine (catecholamine) and Insulin/FSH are membrane-bound, NOT nuclear!

sections.heading: Gametogenesis, Menstrual Cycle & Contraceptives (ART)
sections.summary: Sertoli cells nourish sperms & secrete Inhibin/ABP; Leydig cells secrete Androgens (Testosterone) under LH.
keyPoints: Spermatogenesis: 1 primary spermatocyte (2n) -> 2 secondary (n) -> 4 spermatids (n) -> 4 sperms. Oogenesis: 1 primary oocyte (2n, arrested Dictyate/Diplotene!) -> 1 functional ovum + polar bodies.
Menstrual Day 14 OVULATION triggered strictly by sharp mid-cycle LH SURGE! Luteal phase (~14 days fixed): Corpus Luteum secretes Progesterone maintaining endometrium.

IUDs: Non-medicated (Lippes loop), Cu-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375 -> suppress sperm motility!), Hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20 -> hostile cervix). ART: ZIFT (<= 8 blastomeres -> fallopian tube), IUT (> 8 -> uterus), GIFT (in-vivo).

sections.heading: Evolution: Homology, Adaptive Radiation & Hardy-Weinberg
sections.summary: Homologous = divergent evolution (same ancestor/structure: Forelimbs of whale/bat/cheetah/human; Bougainvillea thorn & Cucurbita tendril); Analogous = convergent (Wings butterfly & bird; Potato stem & Sweet potato root!).
keyPoints: Stanley Miller (1953) spark chamber: CH4 + H2 + NH3 (2:1:2) + water vapour at 800 deg C yielded amino acids (Alanine, Glycine, Aspartic acid).
Darwin's Finches & Australian Marsupials show Adaptive Radiation (convergent marsupial wolf vs placental wolf!).

Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium: p + q = 1 and p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1. Five factors disturb equilibrium: Gene migration/flow, Genetic drift (Founder effect!), Mutation, Recombination, Natural Selection (Stabilizing, Directional, Disruptive).

formulas.note: Always find q = sqrt(q^2 recessive phenotype frequency) FIRST!
Homo habilis = first toolmaker; Neanderthal buried dead & used hides

comparison.title: Gametogenesis & ART Reference
rows: Ovum from donor into recipient unable to produce ovum

traps: Secondary oocyte finishes Meiosis-II ONLY at the exact moment of sperm entry before syngamy!
Sweet potato (root modification) vs Potato (stem tuber) are ANALOGOUS (convergent evolution); Bougainvillea thorns vs Cucurbita tendrils are HOMOLOGOUS!

solvedExamples.question: In a randomly mating population of 1,000 individuals, 90 individuals express an autosomal recessive trait (aa). Find the count of heterozygous carriers (Aa).
steps: Carrier frequency 2pq = 2 x 0.7 x 0.3 = 0.42 => count = 0.42 x 1000 = 420 carriers.

sections.heading: Human Health, Immunity & Industrial Microbes
sections.summary: Innate barriers (Skin, Acid/Lysozyme, NK cells, Interferons) vs Acquired B/T-lymphocyte specificity.
keyPoints: Antibodies (H2L2): IgG (crosses placenta!), IgA (colostrum mucosal immunity), IgE (allergy histamine/mast cells!), IgM (pentamer first responder).
Active Immunity (host makes antibodies, slow, memory: vaccines) vs Passive (ready-made: Colostrum IgA, ATS tetanus serum). ELISA detects HIV; Widal confirms Typhoid (Salmonella typhi).

Microbes: Monascus purpureus -> Statins (blood cholesterol competitive inhibitor!); Trichoderma polysporum -> Cyclosporin A (immunosuppressant!); Aspergillus niger -> Citric acid; BOD measures organic sewage pollution (higher BOD = higher pollution!).

sections.heading: Biotechnology: pBR322, PCR & Transgenic Applications
sections.summary: Type-II Restriction Endonucleases (EcoRI cuts G|AATTC leaving sticky ends) cut DNA at specific palindromic 6-bp sequences.
keyPoints: Gel Electrophoresis separates negatively charged DNA toward ANODE (+), smaller fragments run farther -> Ethidium bromide + UV light visualizes bright orange bands!

pBR322: Selectable markers amp^R (PstI, PvuI) and tet^R (BamHI, SalI); ori controls copy number; rop codes replication proteins. Insertional inactivation of lacZ turns X-gal colonies WHITE (recombinants) vs BLUE (non-recombinants)!
PCR Steps (Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus): Denaturation (94 deg C) -> Annealing (~55 deg C) -> Extension (72 deg C); 2^n copies after n cycles!

Applications: Bt Cotton cry1Ac & cry2Ab control cotton bollworms (alkaline insect midgut activates protoxin!); RNAi Meloidegyne incognitia silencing via Agrobacterium; Eli Lilly Humulin linked A & B chains excluding C-peptide; 1990 ADA deficiency gene therapy.

formulas.note: 30 cycles amplify a single DNA stretch ~1 billion times!

formulas.formula: cryIAc / cryIIAb -> Cotton Bollworm | cryIAb -> Corn Borer
formulas.note: Protoxin crystals stay harmless in Bacillus due to acidic/neutral host pH

comparison.title: Industrial Microbes & Bioactive Products
rows: Clot buster for myocardial infarction patients

traps: Human pro-insulin contains A, B AND C-peptide; MATURE insulin lacks C-peptide completely!
In pBR322, inserting foreign DNA at BamHI destroys Tetracycline resistance (tet^R) while leaving Ampicillin resistance (amp^R) intact!

solvedExamples.question: Foreign DNA is ligated into the BamHI site of plasmid vector pBR322 and transformed into E. coli. How do transformant recombinants behave on Ampicillin vs Tetracycline plates?
steps: BamHI resides strictly inside the tet^R gene, disrupting Tetracycline resistance (insertional inactivation).
amp^R remains untouched -> Recombinants GROW on Ampicillin medium but DIE on Tetracycline medium!
solvedExamples.answer: Grow on Ampicillin, fail on Tetracycline
solvedExamples.pitfall: Non-recombinant plasmids retain BOTH resistances; non-transformants die on both!
